headline: MEXC has paused some USDT withdrawals after the US Treasury moved to cut it off, while bitcoin holds near $76,000 ahead of Tuesday's US inflation report.

stories.title: MEXC pauses some USDT withdrawals after the US Treasury orders a cut-off
stories.summary: The US Treasury's financial-crimes unit, FinCEN, ordered US banks and payment firms to stop handling transfers involving crypto exchange MEXC, alleging billions in illicit flows. On Saturday MEXC paused withdrawals of the USDT stablecoin on several blockchains, calling it routine maintenance, and money has been flowing out of the exchange.
points: FinCEN alleges at least $16B in illicit transactions linked to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, and to cybercrime.
An independent tracker showed only 6 of 18 USDT withdrawal networks working on Saturday; Ethereum still worked while TRON, Solana, BNB Chain, Arbitrum and Polygon were down, per FinanceFeeds.
MEXC saw $126.03M of net outflows over 24 hours, per DefiLlama data cited by cryptonews.net.
The order takes effect 30 days after it is published in the Federal Register, per Cointelegraph.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds near $76,000 in a fearful weekend market
stories.summary: Bitcoin has barely moved on Saturday, and a popular sentiment gauge still reads Fear. Tuesday's US inflation report is the next big data point.
points: Bitcoin was $76,032 on CoinCodex at about 16:00 UTC Saturday, up 0.77% over 24 hours.
Ether was $2,243.40 (up 1.05%) and Solana $89.91 (down 0.80%) on CoinCodex at the same time.
CoinCodex's Fear & Greed Index read 28, labelled Fear.
Forecasters on the Finviz calendar expect October US consumer prices to rise 0.3%, after 0.6% in September; the report is due Tuesday at 8:30am ET.

stories.title: Binance hack: plan to reopen six more withdrawals by end of next week
stories.summary: Binance's Richard Teng confirmed the plan to reopen withdrawals for six more coins by the end of next week. Blockchain analysts at Elliptic say $2.85B of the $6.43B stolen has been frozen, while the hackers convert some of the rest into bitcoin.
points: Binance aims to reopen HYPE, INJ, APT, PLASMA, NEAR and LTC withdrawals by the end of next week, per The Coin Republic.
Binance says it has replaced 98% of the stolen assets, and LTC and NEAR can already be withdrawn as tokens on BNB Chain, per CryptoTicker.
Elliptic puts the theft at $6.43B, with $2.85B verified frozen.
About $124M of stolen tokens has been swapped into bitcoin, per The Block.

briefs.title: Nigeria's new stablecoin rules take effect
briefs.summary: Nigeria's central bank rules took effect on 5 Nov: dollar-stablecoin issuers need ₦15B in capital, exchanges and wallet providers ₦1B, and existing operators have 30 days to register, per Techpoint Africa.

briefs.title: Treasury drops $250 crypto Travel Rule plan
briefs.summary: FinCEN and the Fed withdrew a 2020 proposal to lower the threshold for collecting transfer data from $3,000 to $250, per The Block.

briefs.title: Zcash upgrade cuts block time to 25 seconds
briefs.summary: Zcash's NU7 upgrade went live on 6 Nov at block 3,543,405, cutting the target time between blocks from 75 to 25 seconds, per Bytes Europe.
